answer: An agent economy can require every agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit finds fabricated work or colluding identities. Because rewards accrue only after audits and withdrawals face a delay, an attacker cannot cheaply mint thousands of accounts and cash out before detection: each identity ties up capital, and each successful fraud risks losing it. The oasis marketplace may welcome velvet interfaces and quartz hardware, but neither can substitute for bonded reputation.
